notes: Descriptive questionnaire survey of 384 respondents (128 per agro-ecological zone) in Soin Ward, Kericho, Kenya, classifying agroforestry systems around sugarcane. Only adoption-type figures (shares practising a system or arrangement, shares naming constraints); no costs, returns or carbon income values. Inclusion is borderline: the sample is agroforestry practitioners, so the shares describe the mix of systems among adopters, not adoption rates in the population. fodder_banks (pilot tag) not confirmed: calliandra appears only as a tree preference (0.2%). Not extracted: Tables 3-6 (functional, socio-economic, land-use and 'ecological' classes, which are not practices), tree species preferences, and benefit shares (income 67.6%, employment 24.1%, social amenities) which are shares of respondents naming a benefit, not money values.

adoption.definition_used: practiced a silvopastoral system that was characterised by grazing of domestic animals such as cows on Napier grass pastures
adoption.note: 79 farmers of 384. Paper's description (p8) mentions grazing on Napier pastures but not the tree component; the vocabulary's silvopasture fit is as labelled by the authors. Land-size breakdown cells in Table 2 are shares of the full sample (cross-tab), not rates within land-size classes, so not extracted. Survey year not stated (published October 2022). Respondents were 'agroforestry farmers and households' (p5), so shares are among agroforestry practitioners, not a population adoption rate.

adoption.definition_used: practised agrisilvicultural system of agroforestry that involved planting food crops such as maise, sugarcane and trees in the same land in terms of alley cropping or home gardens
adoption.note: 121 farmers of 384. Borderline practice code: the authors' agrisilviculture includes home gardens (multistrata, out of scope) as well as alley cropping; reviewer to confirm or drop. Agrosilvopastoral (48.2%, 184 farmers) not extracted: it mixes home gardens, livestock and scattered trees on cropland and maps to no single code. Survey year not stated (published October 2022). Respondents were 'agroforestry farmers and households' (p5), so shares are among agroforestry practitioners, not a population adoption rate.
